scenes.title: LEFT JOIN
scenes.narration: A LEFT JOIN returns every row from the left table and attaches matching right-table columns, using NULL where no match exists.

scenes.title: What LEFT JOIN guarantees
bullets: Every row from the left table is kept.
Matching right columns are filled in when found.
Right columns become NULL when there is no match.
scenes.narration: Every row from the left table survives regardless of whether it has a partner. When a match exists the right-side columns are filled with that data. When no match exists those right-side columns are set to NULL, marking the gap.

scenes.title: All customers, even without orders
scenes.code:
SELECT c.customer_name, o.order_id, o.amount
FROM customers AS c
LEFT JOIN orders AS o
  ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;
scenes.narration: This keeps every customer whether or not they have placed an order. Customers with orders appear once per order with the order details filled in. Customers with no orders still appear, but their order_id and amount columns show NULL.

scenes.title: The anti-join pattern
steps: LEFT JOIN the two tables on the key.
Read it as 'left rows with no right match'.
scenes.narration: A powerful trick is the anti-join, which finds left rows that have no counterpart on the right. You left join the tables, then filter with WHERE on the right key being NULL, leaving only the rows where the match failed.

scenes.title: Customers who never ordered
scenes.code:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name
FROM customers AS c
LEFT JOIN orders AS o
  ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.order_id IS NULL;
scenes.narration: Here the left join pairs each customer with their orders, then WHERE keeps only rows where no order was found. Because a missing match produces NULL in the order columns, testing o.order_id IS NULL isolates customers who have never placed an order. This is the standard way to find records that exist in one table but not another.

scenes.title: Match found vs no match

left.title: Match found
points: Right columns filled from matched row.
May produce multiple rows per left row.

scenes.narration: When a match is found the left row carries its own values plus the matched right columns, and it can repeat if several right rows match. When no match is found the left row appears exactly once with NULL in every right column. That NULL is what makes gap detection possible.

scenes.text: Putting a right-table condition in WHERE (instead of ON) can silently turn a LEFT JOIN into an INNER JOIN by filtering out the NULL rows.
scenes.narration: Be careful where you place right-table conditions, because filtering them in WHERE can drop the NULL rows and quietly turn your left join into an inner join.
